unreleased: Add an event_booking module (app/modules/event_booking) for registering for an event, built on the event calendar and forms: a registration belongs to one event and offers slots made from blocks of days (a list of days, weekdays within a range, or any future day) and times (all day, a list, or generated every N minutes) with a capacity per slot - per day for an all-day slot; nothing is stored per slot, they are computed. A visitor books with name, e-mail, consent to the processing of personal data and the form's answers; who may book is public, signed-in only, or by a secret link (a registration reached by link is not mentioned to anyone without it). The capacity is checked under a lock on the registration row, so two people cannot take the last place, and registering is possible only while the registration is open, the article is published and the event is not over. A honeypot field and a limit of upcoming bookings per e-mail address slow spam down (there is no rate limiting). The person gets a confirmation with a link to cancel (a button on a page, never a GET) and the administrator a notice; administrators manage registrations and bookings, can move a booking, correct its name, e-mail and answers or cancel it with a note and an e-mail to the person (in the language they booked in, whose failure is reported and never undoes the change), see the history of changes, export a CSV (formula-safe) and a summary of the answers of confirmed bookings. Bookings are deleted a configurable number of months after their date (default 12), by a purge that runs at most once a day when a booking is made or the list is opened, or on demand. Texts and switches are in backend/modules/event_booking.json, the notice address in BOOKING_NOTIFY_MAIL (else CONTACT_MAIL); tzdata is now a dependency (local times are Europe/Prague)

Add a forms module (app/modules/forms) for other modules to build on: forms with questions of seven types (checkbox, radio, text, number, date, time, date and time), questions shown only when earlier answers say so (several conditions, chaining through hidden questions), validation of the answers on the server with error codes (the regular expression of a text question is run with a time limit, and one that backtracks catastrophically is refused when the form is saved), answers stored as a snapshot of the questions as they were worded when answered, and, for administrators, browsing the answers and a basic summary per question (counts and shares of the options, minimum / maximum / average / median of numbers, earliest and latest dates). The questions of a form are replaced as a whole list, in order; a form that still has answers cannot be deleted

The event calendar module now builds on articles: an event is just a date (or a run of days, with optional times, a title and a description of up to 128 characters) belonging to exactly one article, an article can have several. The wall (/dashboard) is made of articles - the one with the nearest upcoming date, the pinned ones and the last five past ones - the calendar, archive and search follow the article's visibility (archived articles stay findable), and search also looks through the article text ignoring diacritics. GET /by-article/{id} lists an article's dates. Events no longer have their own page, slug, image, status or pinned flag, and image upload moved to the articles module. The database table is recreated: existing events are NOT carried over

Add an articles module (app/modules/articles): articles with a title, perex, sanitized HTML content, image, status (draft / published / archived), optional display window, a pinned flag and a type, plus dynamic article types with frame and background colours for the light and dark theme. Public listing, search ignoring case and diacritics over title, perex and full text (archived articles included, drafts never), detail by slug, and administrator-only management with image upload; a type in use is deleted only with a replacement type

The shared HTML sanitizer now also keeps tables, text alignment, horizontal rules, code blocks and YouTube / Vimeo video embeds; frames from any other address, and anything that could run script, are still removed on every save

A module can declare the modules it requires (`ModuleManifest.requires`); enabling one without them now logs a warning at startup, naming both, instead of failing later in some request. The warning never stops the application

Only administrators can create categories now: POST /categories and POST /categories/check answer 403 {"code": "admin_required"} to anyone else (a blocked account is still told so first, and the auth service's admin role does not count - only the local is_admin flag). Ordinary users keep adding posts to any category, and the categories that already exist are untouched

Contact-form module: GET /api/modules/kontaktni_formular/info serves a per-language page heading, introduction and note (the new `page` block of backend/modules/kontaktni_formular.json) plus public contact details - address, GitHub and LinkedIn links from CONTACT_ADDRESS / CONTACT_GITHUB_URL / CONTACT_LINKEDIN_URL in .env, and the delivery address only when `show_email` is on. Nothing is shown until it is configured

Add a CRM module (app/modules/crm), for administrators only: partners with contact and company details, their tasks (status, price, dates), and invoice PDFs uploaded against a task - checked to really be PDFs and capped at 10 MB, stored privately under uploads/crm/ and served only to administrators through an authenticated download

A post's value is never below zero, and the floor applies to the calculation too: an old post that nobody paid for or resonated with is worth 0, and the next resonance or payment shows in full at once (one resonance on an old post makes it 1, a $5 payment makes it 50) instead of being eaten by the age the post had already "lost" below zero. A new floor_lift column on posts records what the floor has forgiven (run alembic upgrade head; existing posts are unaffected); only a resonance or a payment ever changes it, and the board's ordering includes it, so posts that all show 0 stay ordered by what they have actually earned

Payments no longer switch themselves off in silence: when the backend starts it now writes one warning to the console that lists every reason payments are off (the gateway module not enabled, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY or STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET missing, the provider's details incomplete in boards.json) and which file to change - or says they are on - and administrators get the same list from GET /manage/payments-status. Only whether a key is set is ever reported, never its value. A module can now declare an on_startup hook in its manifest; a hook that fails is logged and does not stop the application

Authors can hide their own posts and show them again: POST /me/posts/{id}/hide takes a published post off the boards (status "hidden"), POST /me/posts/{id}/show puts it back. Nothing else changes - it keeps what was paid for it and its resonances, nobody is refunded, and its value keeps falling with age while hidden (a post that is shown again is not made young again). Hiding twice is harmless; somebody else's post is a 404; a blocked account gets 403; a blocked or removed post cannot be hidden or shown (409). A hidden post can still be blocked by an administrator, is taken down with a blocked account, and cannot be paid for until it is shown; administrators can find hidden posts (status "hidden") but cannot restore them

Authors get a payment overview: GET /me/payments lists every payment they started for their posts, newest first and whatever became of it (pending, paid, failed, expired), with the post's title and state today, whether its category is blocked, and the document issued for it, plus a summary of what they have actually paid (completed payments only, over every page). A blocked or removed post keeps what was paid, which the overview says plainly

Administrators can undo a block: POST /manage/posts/{id}/restore publishes a blocked (or removed) post again with what was paid for it and its resonances, tells the author, and stops counting it as a violation - so withdrawing a mistaken block also keeps the author's account clear of the strike limit. It is refused (409 author_blocked) while the author's account is blocked, since a published post of a blocked account would contradict the block; unblock the account first

Administrators can block a whole category and restore it: GET /manage/categories lists every category (blocked ones included) with filters, POST /manage/categories/{slug}/block takes a reason the creator is notified with, POST .../restore puts it back as it was. A blocked category is gone for visitors (not listed, 404, nothing can be posted, checked, resonated with or paid for in it) but nothing in it is changed or deleted, its posts keep what was paid for them, and it is no strike for anybody; its address stays taken. Posts now say whether their category is blocked (GET /me/posts, the administrators' post list)

Every confirmed payment now gets a document and a confirmation email: a numbered receipt (2026-000001, gapless within a year, stored as an unchangeable snapshot in the same transaction that raises the post's value) is emailed to the payer in their language once the payment is committed, with the contract confirmation and the terms link; a failed email is recorded and retried (with the next confirmed payment, or by an administrator at POST /manage/receipts/retry) and never touches the payment. Payers read their documents at GET /me/receipts. Payments are refused until the provider's details are filled in (backend/modules/boards.json, invoicing), and a test keeps them equal to the ones on the legal pages

The payment gateway keeps the payer's email with the payment and lets a payment purpose run an after_paid hook once the payment is safely committed (once per payment, its failure never undoes the payment) - the place for a confirmation email

Authors can pay to raise the value of their own posts: a whole number of USD from 1 to 500 per payment (backend/modules/boards.json), priced and checked on the server (the post must be theirs and still published, the account not blocked), added atomically to the post once Stripe confirms - so payments accumulate and 1 USD becomes 10 points. Posts now tell their own author so (`mine`, with what was paid), GET /me/posts lists a user's own posts in every state, GET /payments says whether payments are on, and the payment gateway is switched on

A payment purpose can now require consents (PaymentPurpose.required_consents): a checkout that lacks one is refused with 422 before anything is created or sent to Stripe, so a request that skips the pay button cannot skip the express request for immediate performance either

Switch on the contact form module (kontaktni_formular) for ThoughtAuction with its confirmation email carrying the application's name, and add a test that keeps the numbers the public terms quote (points per USD, check thresholds, strike limit and period, text limits) equal to what the boards module enforces

The content check now explains to the author only the aspects behind a score that is over the warning threshold - no more faint "does not fit the category" under a verdict about vulgar language; administrators still get every finding with the stored post

Boards are now moderated end to end: every new post and category is checked before it is published (refused above 75 %, published only on the author's explicit confirmation above 50 %, with POST .../check to see the verdict and its aspects first), a new category gets machine rules built from its title and description, administrators (the local is_admin flag) can find any post under /manage, block it with a reason - removed without refund, the author notified through the notifications module - read, edit and rebuild a category's machine rules, and an author whose posts are blocked 3 times within 30 days (backend/modules/boards.json) has the account blocked and the remaining posts removed, until an administrator unblocks it

Add the boards module's local content checks (app/modules/boards/moderation): a violation score in percent (profanity, insults, hate, threats, link spam, personal data, shouting, repetition - seeing through spaced-out letters, digits and stretched letters) and a topic-mismatch score against a category's machine rules (keywords built from its title and description), each with the specific aspects behind it and warn / risk / block levels above 30 / 50 / 75 %, plus a prepared-but-mock-only AI review contract, all tunable in backend/modules/boards.json

Add a boards module (app/modules/boards): publication boards (categories) with a generated slug and a short description, and posts ordered by value - paid USD x 10 + resonances - days of age, computed on read and never exposing the author or who resonated; reading is public, while creating a board, posting (title + text up to 2048 characters) and resonating (once per user and post) need a signed-in user
